answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a crystal as the anchor of the cost.
